## ContactsAccountCapability.max_address_books_per_card is Option<u32>; RFC 9610 UnsignedInt and every sibling capability limit is u64
Crates: jmap-contacts-types
Evidence: crate-jmap-contacts-types/src/capability.rs:33 `pub max_address_books_per_card: Option<u32>`. RFC 9610 L150 (/home/mark/PROJECT/IETF/specs/rfc9610.txt): "*maxAddressBooksPerCard*: UnsignedInt|null" (RFC 8620 §1.3 UnsignedInt is 0..2^53-1). Analogous per-object-container limits in sibling account capabilities are all Option<u64>: MailAccountCapability.max_mailboxes_per_email (crate-jmap-mail-types/src/capability.rs, canonical), CalendarsAccountCapability.max_calendars_per_event (crate-jmap-calendars-types/src/capability.rs), TasksAssigneesAccountCapability.max_participants_per_task, SceneCapability/VtcCapability max_* (Option<u64>). A sweep of pub integer fields in every *-types crate finds no other capability limit narrower than u64. No bead found (bd search maxAddressBooksPerCard / max_address_books_per_card: none).
Why breaking later: Changing a pub field type on a published struct is a semver break: readers that bind it as Option<u32> (or compare it against u32 values) stop compiling. Until it changes, a server advertising any value above u32::MAX (e.g. 2^53-1 as an effectively unlimited value, which is legal UnsignedInt) makes serde_json::from_value::<ContactsAccountCapability> fail, so the client fails to decode the whole account capability instead of reading a large limit.
Fix: Change the field to Option<u64> before 0.4, matching MailAccountCapability.max_mailboxes_per_email; update the two unit tests in crate-jmap-contacts-types/src/lib.rs (around 652/665) to keep using hand-written JSON fixtures. Nothing else in the workspace reads the field.
Size: S
